questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] Why do soccer players spit so much during games?
A. To clear mucus from their mouths
B. Because they drink a lot of water
C. To relieve stress
Answer: A. Intense physical activity increases the protein content in saliva, making it thicker and more uncomfortable for the players, leading them to spit to clear their mouths.
questions.de: Was geschieht bei intensiver körperlicher Belastung mit dem Speichel, sodass Fußballspieler so oft spucken?
questions.en: What happens to saliva during intense exercise that makes football players spit so often?
questions.answerDe: Er wird dicker und eiweißreicher (Mucin MUC5B) und lässt sich schwer schlucken
questions.answerEn: It gets thicker, with more protein (mucin MUC5B), so it is hard to swallow

timeline.labelEn: Dutch study shows that running raises the secretion of the mucin MUC5B in saliva
timeline.labelDe: Niederländische Studie zeigt, dass Laufen die Ausschüttung des Mucins MUC5B im Speichel erhöht

source.title: Why do football players spit so much?

questions.notes: Card consistent with BBC Science Focus: exercise raises salivary protein, especially the mucus MUC5B, making saliva thicker and harder to swallow. Timeline: Ligtenberg et al., Archives of Oral Biology 60(11), 2015.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is the only animal known to perform surgical amputations?
A. Ants B. Bees C. Spiders
Answer: A. Florida carpenter ants have been observed performing surgical amputations on their nestmates. When an ant’s leg is severely injured, other ants may chew off the affected leg to prevent infection and save their nestmate.
questions.de: Welche Ameisenart amputiert – als einziges bekanntes Tier außer dem Menschen – verletzte Beine ihrer Nestgenossinnen, um Infektionen aufzuhalten?
questions.en: Which ant species, apart from humans the only animal known to do so, amputates the injured legs of its nestmates to stop infections spreading?

timeline.labelEn: Study in Current Biology reports Florida carpenter ants amputating nestmates' injured legs
timeline.labelDe: Studie in Current Biology beschreibt, wie Florida-Rossameisen verletzte Beine von Nestgenossinnen amputieren

questions.notes: 'Only animal' means apart from humans (Frank et al., Current Biology, July 2024). Amputation is chosen for femur injuries; tibia wounds are cleaned instead.
